To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current copyright regime does not address the advent of sophisticated online AI translation systems, which have been developed in the past few years, and which have the potential to become ubiquitous and to transform the way humans communicate.

(1) The current copyright regime does not adequately address the use of AI systems, and particularly AI translation systems, in the 3As Era; (2) AI translation systems are prone to algorithmic biases, which may perpetuate sexist and racist expressions, and other objectionable expressions; (3) The current legal regime does not adequately recognize the concerns of authors whose work is translated using AI systems; and (4) The current copyright legal regime does not provide a sufficient balance between the benefits
AI translation systems are not only a blessing for the world of communication, but that they also have a number of shortcomings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the legal and ethical issues that arise in the use of AI systems in translation, and how to address them in the current legal regime.
the legal and social implications of the use of AI systems for translation.
the legal and policy issues that arise when AI translation systems are used for personal or commercial translation
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the legal regime should be modified to include AI translation systems and to recognize their benefits and shortcomings, while at the same time, recognizing the integrity of the author's linguistic choices.

this Article calls on the legal and academic community to recognize and address the shortcomings of the current copyright regime and to adopt a new approach, one that would allow for the harmonization of AI technology and copyright law, in order to promote access to an advanced technology that has the potential to revolutionize human communications across the world.

the current copyright law is outdated and ill equipped for the advent of sophisticated artificial intelligence online translation tools. A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the current legal and academic communities have failed to address the advent of AI translation systems in the copyright regime, and that the present inability for AI technology to routinely and reliably capture the nuance and beauty of human prose gives us pause to reflect on the concerns of authors and their rights to control the linguistic integrity of their works and their right to object to unauthorized AI translation.
the Article calls for an international standardization of guidelines for the use and implementation of AI translation systems.
we have to find a balance between the benefits and risks of AI translation systems.

policymakers should consider the concerns raised in this article when drafting and adopting AI-related policies, and should consider the suggested principles as a way to balance the interests at stake.
